note: Democrats' sweep moves oil and Washington; the fridge attacks reach French blood plasma; Belgium's government waits on the King.

weather.now: 3 °C and clear at 05:00, east-northeast wind 2, no warnings
weather.weekNote: Dry and sunny to Sunday, fog possible on Saturday morning, wetter from Tuesday. [1, 2]

items.t: AFNORTH **12:30 release**, second day of parent conferences. [3]
Bank of England at 13:00 CET, a first hike to 4% widely expected; the White House hosts Russian and Ukrainian representatives on Oleshky at 17:00 CET. [4, 5]
A4 toward Köln: one lane between Eschweiler-West and Eschweiler-Ost, 19:00–05:00. Canes at the Islanders, Fri 01:00 CET. [6, 7]
Posture options due to Hegseth; Belgium's King sees De Wever at 10:30; US payrolls 14:30 CET; Sint Maarten parade in Brunssum's Langeberg. [8, 9, 10, 11]

five.t: **Trump asked advisers whether Hegseth should stay,** then called his work “a very good job”; the Europe posture options reach Hegseth tomorrow.
**Oil fell 8.7% to $94.62 and the Dow rose 3.0%** as traders read the Democratic sweep as a push toward an Iran deal; Khamenei warned against any “inclination towards surrender”.
**The fridge attacks reached France's blood plasma stores;** a Scottish firm puts Russian involvement at “about 95 percent”, Romania's cyber chief rules out a state actor.
**SACEUR warned Warsaw about Kaliningrad,** Tusk says; Poland moved police, counter-terror units and border guards to the north-east.
**Belgium's government hangs on a royal meeting on Friday;** the King has held De Wever's resignation since Monday's budget collapse.

pick.t: If you read one thing: the plasma-store lead. The cold-chain attacks have moved from groceries to blood, which puts them inside baseline requirement 5.

items.h: Brussels talks turn to post-war money; the Komyshuvakha toll reaches 40
items.body: The European Commission hosted Ukraine, the United States, Germany, France, Britain, NATO and the World Bank on 4 Nov on “post-war economic development” scenarios. [12] Rustem Umerov said they worked on the Prosperity Plan and Ukraine's 2027 war funding: “We are not disclosing details yet. Substantive work on the document is underway.” [13] After a call with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, President Zelensky said: “We are preparing for a trilateral format at the team level between Ukraine, the United States, and Russia.” [14] Zelensky put the toll of the 2 Nov bombing in Komyshuvakha at 40, with more than 30 people possibly still under rubble; Kyiv had its worst water outage of the war after the 3 Nov strikes on the power system. [15, 16]
items.next: Talks on security guarantees continue in Brussels today; the White House event on Oleshky is at 11:00 ET (17:00 CET) today; Abu Dhabi on 10–11 Nov. [13, 5, 17]

items.h: Khamenei calls US power in decline; the IRGC claims four tankers hit by mines
items.body: In a written message for the anniversary of the 1979 embassy seizure on 4 Nov, Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei said US power is in “irreversible decline” and that “the slightest inclination towards surrender will embolden the arrogant enemy.” Parliament speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf wrote on X: “Conscience or the cost of living, Americans said NO TO WAR, and we endorse this message.” [18] The Revolutionary Guards (IRGC) claim, through IRNA, that four tankers struck mines in a prohibited lane south of the strait and that they downed a US MQ-9 drone; US Central Command has not commented. [19, 20] President Trump told the Financial Times: “We seem to be getting everything we want.” [20]
items.next: Qatar says it is facilitating a “real-time exchange of proposals”; no reply to its draft has been published and no date is set for direct talks. [20, 21]

items.h: AP calls the Senate for Democrats; Mississippi and Alaska are still counting
items.body: AP called the Senate for Democrats late on 3 Nov. [22] By CNBC's count on 4 Nov, Democrats flipped seven Republican Senate seats and at least 24 House seats, and Republicans flipped none. [23] In Mississippi Scott Colom led Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith by 1,138 votes, 464,926 to 463,788; in Alaska Mary Peltola led Sen. Dan Sullivan by 626 votes with about 74% counted. [24, 25] Vice President JD Vance wrote on X: “The reason we lost is the war.” [26]
items.next: Mississippi resolves provisional ballots by 10 Nov; Alaska's ranked-choice count is set for 18 Nov if no candidate passes 50%; the lame-duck Congress returns on 9 Nov. [25, 27]

items.h: North Korea tests a new air-defence missile; 19 PLA aircraft cross the median line
items.body: KCNA said on 5 Nov that the Missile Administration tested a “new-type anti-aircraft missile system” on 4 Nov under Kim Jong Sik, and that a strategic cruise missile subunit “flawlessly carried out the strike mission against a hypothetical airfield target”. South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff (JCS) had detected several missiles from the Sondok area flying less than 300 km that morning. [28, 29] Kim Yo Jong said on 4 Nov that “the options for safeguarding peace certainly include dialogue”. [30] Taiwan counted 21 Chinese military aircraft sorties in the 24 hours to 06:00 on 5 Nov, 19 across the median line. [31]
items.next: Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) leaders meet in Shenzhen on 18–19 Nov.

items.h: Drones hit Sudan's grid again; fighting returns to Masisi
items.body: Radio Dabanga reports drone strikes on two power stations in Kassala and a substation at Merowe on 3 Nov, and drone attacks that killed eight people in Um Dibo, West Kordofan, on 2 Nov and at least four at a fuel station in El Abbasiya Tagali, South Kordofan, on 3 Nov. UN spokesman Stéphane Dujarric said the Secretary-General “strongly condemned the escalating drone attacks by parties to the conflict.” [32] In Yemen a Houthi ballistic missile hit the al-Jumaima training camp in al-Dhalea, killing eight, a military source told Al Jazeera. [33] In eastern Congo the army (FARDC) and allied Wazalendo fighters attacked M23 positions in Masisi from 3 Nov; local sources told Radio Okapi at least four civilians were killed. [34]
items.next: MONUSCO's mandate expires in December; its head, James Swan, has been in Goma since 2 Nov. [35]

feature.title: North Korea's month of launches, 6 Oct to 5 Nov
body: In the 30 days to 5 Nov, South Korea's Joint Chiefs of Staff and North Korea's state agency KCNA reported launches or weapons tests on six days, and South Korea flew its first hypersonic glide vehicle on 8 Oct, with President Lee Jae Myung watching. [36] On 12 Oct North Korea fired ballistic missiles from the Pyongyang area; the JCS said one flew more than 900 km, and Japan's defence ministry counted two, of about 220 km and more than 900 km. KCNA called it a “tactical ballistic missile” test that “verified a technical upgrade”. [37]

On 14 Oct a submarine fired two types of cruise missile, and Missile Administration director Jang Chan Ha said it was “hard to believe” that the South's glide vehicle had flown at hypersonic speed. [36] On 29 Oct, at about 12:30 local time, about 10 short-range ballistic missiles flew about 250 km from the Wonsan area, the JCS said. [38]

The tempo rose in the last week. KCNA reported a tactical ballistic missile with a cluster warhead on 31 Oct and strategic cruise missiles with a dispersal warhead on 2 Nov. [39, 40] On 4 Nov the JCS detected several missiles from Sondok flying under 300 km, and KCNA said that day's tests were a new anti-aircraft missile system and a cruise missile drill against a simulated airfield. [28]
timeline: South Korea flies its first hypersonic glide vehicle.

KCNA: strategic cruise missiles tested with a dispersal warhead.

after: The JCS announced the launches of 12 Oct, 29 Oct and 4 Nov; the 31 Oct and 2 Nov tests are known only from KCNA, and Seoul announced neither. Ranges are as the JCS and Japan's defence ministry gave them, converted from miles where outlets reported miles. [37, 39, 40]

incidents.place: France: three EFS plasma cold stores (sites not named; marker at EFS headquarters, Saint-Denis)
incidents.text: Temperature and defrost thresholds were raised to “extremely high levels” through refrigeration supplier Coolworld, which blames a third-party component; alarms caught it and the blood service says no products were compromised. France's cyber agency ANSSI and the health ministry are investigating. [41, 42]

incidents.place: United Kingdom: small meat-processing firms (not named; marker at Birmingham)
incidents.text: Richard Horne, chief executive of the National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC), said hackers tried to target small meat processors with minimal impact and that “vulnerable technology had been exploited” in a couple of cases. [43]

leads.title: The fridge attacks reach France's blood plasma
leads.teaser: Three plasma stores were pushed toward 110 °C through a refrigeration supplier and alarms caught it. Attribution claims now point three ways.
rows: On 2 Nov temperature and defrost thresholds at three plasma cold stores of the French blood service (EFS) were raised to “extremely high levels”; Le Canard Enchaîné reported a change from about −30 °C to 110 °C. Alarms caught it, and EFS says no blood products or samples were compromised. [41, 42]
The intrusion came through refrigeration supplier Coolworld, which says the flaw sat in a third-party component “outside Coolworld's direct control”. [41]

RetailDetail counts 76 Belgian and 17 Dutch stores hit without naming its source; Italy reports about 20 and Romania six. [44, 43] Four commissaries in Germany and England had refrigeration outages in late September, which the Defense Commissary Agency puts down to equipment failure and parts delays. [45]

A0. The Scottish firm Lupovis logged 256 break-in attempts on a decoy Danfoss controller from 91 sources between 20 and 30 Oct, some from infrastructure it links to Russian state groups; its chief executive, Xavier Bellekens, puts it at “about 95 percent”. [46] Dan Cîmpean of Romania's cyber directorate called the attack “semi-amateurish”: “We do not suspect, under any circumstances, that it is a state actor.” [43] Two former US officials told NPR on 3 Nov that some evidence points to Iran. [47]
EU spokesperson Thomas Regnier: “These are not isolated incidents.” [43]
leads.sw: Blood plasma falls under baseline requirement 5 (mass casualties): ask the medical planners which NATO and host-nation blood and pharmacy stores in our area use remote-managed refrigeration, and who can cut that access at night.

leads.title: SACEUR's warning moves Polish police to the Kaliningrad line
leads.teaser: Tusk says Grynkewich warned of possible hostile activity; border guards then saw people with lights near Sępopol who went back across.
rows: Prime Minister Donald Tusk told a cabinet meeting in Warsaw that Gen. Grynkewich had warned Poland of possible hostile activity in the north-east; Poland sent extra police, counter-terror units and border-security personnel there on 2 Nov. [48]
Late on 3 Nov border guards near Sępopol saw people with flashlights close to the border; they withdrew into the Kaliningrad oblast without crossing, broadcaster RMF reported. [48]
A0: no actor named and no crossing.
Grynkewich's line in Warsaw in October: “If someone is foolish enough to attack us, we will fight.” [48]
leads.sw: Poland's north-east is in JFC Brunssum's area: a SACEUR warning acted on through national police is the below-threshold response the regional plans assume, so make sure the readout reaches the J2 and the Polish liaison cell.

pattern: **Health joins food:** the refrigeration route reached France's blood plasma through a supplier's third-party component, after supermarkets in more than ten countries. [41]
**Attribution splits three ways:** a private firm points to Russia, Romania's cyber chief rules out a state actor, and former US officials pointed to Iran. [46, 43, 47]
**The arson network loses an alleged organiser:** German police hold a man accused of sending two men to burn a Starlink station in Poland. [49]
tracker: EU spokesperson: “not isolated incidents”; Commission crisis meetings with ENISA and Europol

hybrid.note: Within 100 km of Heerlen there is no confirmed case: RetailDetail's 17 Dutch and 76 Belgian stores are not named. [44]

europe.h: Belgium's King holds De Wever's resignation and sees him again on Friday
europe.body: Prime Minister Bart De Wever offered his government's resignation to King Philippe on 2 Nov after the five-party coalition failed to agree a budget. [50] The King has kept the decision in suspense, has met the coalition party leaders since Tuesday and sees De Wever again on Friday at 10:30; the Palace regretted the lack of a budget agreement “crédible et à la hauteur des défis actuels”, credible and equal to the present challenges. [9] Without a budget Belgium runs on provisional twelfths, each month at a twelfth of this year's spending. [50]
europe.sw: SHAPE and NATO headquarters sit in Belgium; a budget on provisional twelfths holds Belgian spending at this year's level, so new defence commitments wait for a government.

europe.h: European diplomats greet the midterm result with relief and caution
europe.body: A senior EU diplomat told AFP: “There is relief here that this is the beginning of the end of the Trump era and nobody is happier than Europeans.” Another said: “If anything the US will turn even more inwards.” Allies await the Pentagon's review of US forces in Europe in December, AFP reports. [51] Roberta Haar of Maastricht University told L1 the shift matters for the NATO headquarters in Brunssum. [52]
europe.sw: The option sets reach Hegseth tomorrow and the review closes in December, before the new Congress sits; European relief does not change that sequence.

europe.h: Colby and Duffey head to Poland as Warsaw waits on a base answer
europe.body: The Department of War says Under Secretaries Elbridge Colby (policy) and Michael Duffey (acquisition and sustainment) are travelling to Poland to meet the “Bergen Group” in Kraków; it gave no dates or agenda. [53] Defence24 described the permanent-base request on 4 Nov as still at the stage of “negotiations and political consultations”, for a site in western Poland. [54]
europe.sw: Colby is the Pentagon's policy chief: a Polish offer to host and pay for a base is in front of him in the week the Europe options reach Hegseth.

europe.h: Germany arrests the alleged organiser of the Starlink arson in Poland
europe.body: Police arrested a Turkish national in the Reutlingen district, accused of preparing a terrorist offence by sending two men from Germany to set fire to a Starlink ground station in Poland on 23 Sep. Warsaw suspects Russian intelligence. [49]
europe.sw: Arsonists recruited in one country to strike in another is the proxy pattern host-nation police see first; ask how German and Polish case files reach NATO's counter-intelligence staff.

euregio.h: Oirsbeek's Provincialeweg Zuid reopens on Friday, two months early
euregio.body: The roadworks in Oirsbeek, about 8 km from Heerlen, finish on Fri 6 Nov, more than two months ahead of schedule, and Arriva's buses return to their normal route. [55]
euregio.fy: The detour through Oirsbeek ends on Friday.

euregio.h: Heerlen closes its central square from Friday for the carnival opening
euregio.body: For Aod op Nuj on Tue 10 Nov, which the council expects to draw about 7,500 people, the Burgemeester van Grunsvenplein is closed to traffic from Fri 6 Nov 08:00 to Thu 12 Nov 16:00 and the Geerstraat from 18:00 on Tuesday to 01:30. Entry is free. [56]
euregio.fy: Avoid driving through Heerlen centre on Tuesday evening.

items.h: Germany and Lithuania sign a deeper defence pact as Brigade 45 grows
items.body: Defence Ministers Boris Pistorius and Robertas Kaunas signed a declaration of intent on military and industrial cooperation at the Berlin Security Conference on 4 Nov; Brigade 45 “Litauen” is planned at about 4,800 soldiers and 200 civilians, fully ready at the end of 2027. [57] Pistorius: “Ein Angriff auf Litauen wäre ein Angriff auf uns alle”, an attack on Lithuania would be an attack on us all. [58]
items.sw: Brigade 45 is in JFC Brunssum's area; its end-2027 readiness date is the one to hold German force offers against.

items.h: NATO's military chair: “We are not at war, but we are certainly not at peace”
items.body: Adm. Giuseppe Cavo Dragone, Chair of the NATO Military Committee, told the Berlin Security Conference on 4 Nov: “We are not at war, but we are certainly not at peace.” Lt Gen Remigijus Baltrėnas, Director General of the International Military Staff: “A key aspect of countering hybrid actions is the resilience of societies, as it is by itself a deterrent.” [59]
items.sw: Baltrėnas's line is the case for the seven baseline requirements in one sentence; use it when resilience planning competes with combat lines for staff time.

items.h: The Bundestag releases six procurement packages, including weapons for Heron TP
items.body: The Bundestag budget committee approved six submissions over €25 million on 4 Nov: more weapons for the Heron TP drone, troposcatter radios for the TaWAN tactical network, a Eurofighter radar retrofit, night sights, Role 2 medical facilities and 30 mm training rounds. The ministry gave no values or quantities. [60]
items.sw: Armed Heron TP and troposcatter links add to the German sensing and command picture that feeds the regional plans.

items.h: Lithuania weighs a state drone company and buys Finnish sea mines
items.body: Defence Minister Robertas Kaunas told BNS on 4 Nov: “The idea is to create a state-owned drone holding company”; he gave no budget or timeline. [61] Lithuania's Defence Materiel Agency signed with Forcit Defence for Blocker naval mines under the ten-nation Naval Mines Cooperation; value and quantities were not disclosed. [62]
items.sw: Baltic mine stocks shape the sea-denial part of the regional plans.

items.h: Rheinmetall cuts its 2026 forecast again as the Boxer order slips
items.body: Rheinmetall now guides 2026 sales of about €13.2 billion, down from €13.7–14.2 billion, and an operating margin of about 18.5%, Reuters reported on 4 Nov. Third-quarter sales were €3.15 billion against €2.31 billion a year earlier, with operating profit up 62% to €553 million. The company cites no Arminius Boxer award in 2026, slower batch approvals for artillery ammunition and less revenue from new lines, including its drone cooperation with Destinus. [63]
items.sw: Slower batch approvals hold back 155 mm deliveries the capability targets count on; ask the J4 how German ammunition delivery dates have moved.

items.h: Poland starts building its first guided-rocket factory
items.body: Construction began on 4 Nov in Gorzów Wielkopolski on a plant run by Hanwha WB Advanced System, a venture of Hanwha Aerospace and WB Group, to make rockets for the Homar-K launcher under a contract worth about PLN 14 billion signed on 29 Dec 2025. Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz: “Dzisiaj rozpoczynamy kolejny etap tego przedsięwzięcia”, today we start the next stage of this undertaking. [64]
items.sw: Homar-K is the long-range fires backbone of Polish divisions in JFC Brunssum's area; domestic rockets from 2030 change the sustainment plan, not the 2027 one.

items.h: Helsing hands Germany the source code for its combat-drone mission software
items.body: Helsing gave the procurement office BAAINBw the source code, documentation and a software development kit for MissionOSBw, the mission operating system at the core of the CFSN programme, on 4 Nov; the code is government-owned open source. CFSN, worth more than €220 million and approved in July, covers two experimental uncrewed combat aircraft, two ground stations, autonomy software and a reference architecture, with Hensoldt, Rohde & Schwarz, MBDA and Diehl Defence. [65]
items.sw: Government-owned mission code is the model to cite when allied autonomy software has to work inside a NATO headquarters' network.

items.h: OpenAI's pipeline found 948 Linux kernel privilege-escalation flaws
items.body: OpenAI reported on 4 Nov that a prototype pipeline built on an unreleased cyber model scanned about 2.8 million lines of the Linux kernel in mid-October and produced 1,169 working local privilege-escalation exploits, 948 of them unique, for $1,213,430 in API credits, about $1,279 each. So far 61 are patched upstream and 43 have patches in staging. [66, 67]

items.h: Cognition ships SWE-2 Flash at a fifth of SWE-2's price
items.body: Cognition released SWE-2 Flash on 4 Nov, a coding model with 276 billion parameters, 12 billion active, built from Thinking Machines' Inkling-Small. It runs at about 200 tokens a second against 60 for SWE-2 and costs a fifth as much; it scores 24.0 on FrontierCode 2.0 against SWE-2's 23.8 but 60.1 on DeepSWE 1.1 against 73.0. The weights are withheld over cyber risk. [68]

items.h: Tencent releases Hy4 and holds back the weights
items.body: Tencent released its Hy4 model on 4 Nov, Reuters reported, limited its cyber training to defensive uses and plans to publish the weights later with a safety-testing report: “We recognise the potential safety risks posed by advanced cyber and biological capabilities.” No parameter count or benchmark was published. [69]

cards.n: No nominee for either; no nomination record updated since 31 Oct. [70]
Trump on 4 Nov, after CBS reported he asked advisers whether Hegseth should stay. [71, 72]
Both poised to chair from 3 Jan; Smith promises “vigorous oversight”. [73, 74]
Autonomous and counter-drone systems delivered this year, the DRPM-UxS says. [75]

words.role: Ranking member, House Armed Services Committee (HASC)
words.where: Statement on HASC Democrats' priorities for the 120th Congress
words.quote: the top priority will be to conduct vigorous oversight of the Department of Defense and the Trump Administration
words.context: He also wants to re-establish an Oversight and Investigations Subcommittee and wrote that “the illegal war against Iran is top of mind”. [74]

words.where: Remarks to reporters, asked whether he was considering replacing Secretary Hegseth
words.quote: No, I think he's doing a very good job.
words.context: Reported by CBS News and Reuters on 4 Nov, after CBS said he had asked advisers whether Hegseth should stay. [71, 72]

dod.h: Trump backs Hegseth after asking advisers whether he should stay
dod.body: CBS News reported on 4 Nov, citing multiple sources, that President Trump had asked advisers whether Secretary Hegseth should stay after the midterm losses, and that some White House aides expect part of the blame to fall on Adm. Brad Cooper of CENTCOM and Gen. Dan Caine. [71] Asked the same day whether he was considering replacing Hegseth, Trump said: “No, I think he's doing a very good job.” [72] The option sets on US force levels in Europe are due to Hegseth on 6 Nov; none had leaked by this morning. [8]
dod.sw: The Europe options land on a Secretary whose tenure the President was asked about this week; a cut below the 76,000-troop floor still needs the plan Congress requires first.

dod.h: More than 25,000 drones and counter-drone systems reached CENTCOM this year
dod.body: The Direct Reporting Portfolio Manager for Unmanned Systems (DRPM-UxS) says it delivered more than 25,000 autonomous and counter-unmanned systems to the CENTCOM area this year, under Project Agincourt and the drone dominance effort. [75, 76] AUTOWARCOM still has no commander nominee; Todd Harrison of the American Enterprise Institute told Defense One: “I think AUTOWARCOM is something they can do without Congress.” [77]
dod.sw: CENTCOM fields counter-drone kit by the thousand; ask what share of the DRPM-UxS pipeline is earmarked for EUCOM before the next drone sighting over a base in Europe.

dod.h: The Iran war toll reaches 23 US dead and 866 wounded
dod.body: Defense Casualty Analysis System figures reported by Military Times on 4 Nov count 23 US deaths and 866 wounded since 28 Feb: 15 deaths and 417 wounded in Operation Epic Fury, which the department counts as concluded, and 8 deaths and 449 wounded in overseas operations since 7 Jul. [78]
dod.sw: Smith has put the Iran war at the top of his oversight list; these are the figures the committees will start from.

news.h: Wiesbaden soldiers who missed meals in the DFAC closure can claim the money back
news.body: The Clay Kaserne dining facility in Wiesbaden closed on 30 Sep after fibreglass dust from renovation work and partly reopened on 11 Oct; the closure coincided with Avenger Triad 26. Soldiers on meal cards who missed meals can file reimbursement claims. [79]
news.sw: Dust closed the headquarters dining facility during USAREUR-AF's largest exercise of the autumn: a line for any garrison continuity review.

congress.h: Reed and Smith are poised to chair the Armed Services committees
congress.body: With Democrats in control from 3 Jan, Breaking Defense reports that Sen. Jack Reed is poised to lead the Senate Armed Services Committee (SASC), Rep. Adam Smith the House committee and Sen. Chris Coons Senate defence appropriations. [73] Smith's 4 Nov statement promises “vigorous oversight” and a budget approach that “does not require a defense budget in excess of $1 trillion”. [74] In the lame duck, the FY2027 NDAA (H.R. 8800) still sits in the Senate, where it was received on 14 Sep, and Lt. Gen. Kevin Admiral's nomination to USAREUR-AF (PN1188) is still Calendar No. 924. [80, 81]
congress.sw: The lame-duck NDAA is the last bill the current chairs write; from January Reed and Smith can question the Europe options and the 76,000-troop floor.

items.h: Federal benefits open season runs to 14 Dec, TRICARE's to 8 Dec
items.body: OPM puts the Federal Benefits Open Season, which covers FEDVIP dental and vision, at 9 Nov to 14 Dec; TRICARE's open season runs 9 Nov to 8 Dec. [82, 83]
items.fy: Doing nothing keeps current enrolments; decide on dental and vision before 14 Dec and on TRICARE before 8 Dec.

items.h: The 2027 raise rides on a lame-duck deal
items.body: The House bill gives 7% to E-1 to E-5, 6% to E-6 to O-3 and 5% to O-4 and above; the Senate's gives 3.6% across the board. [84] The IRS had not published 2027 TSP limits by 4 Nov; the 2026 deferral limit is $24,500. [85]
items.fy: Hold January TSP changes until the IRS notice; for a field-grade officer the bills differ by 5% against 3.6% of base pay.

aperture.contrarian: Markets read the Democratic sweep as a road to an Iran deal: Andy Lipow said the result leads traders “to conclude that Trump might now be inclined to make a deal”. [86] Tehran's answer points the other way: Khamenei warned that “the slightest inclination towards surrender will embolden the arrogant enemy”, and the IRGC claims four more tankers hit by mines. [18, 19] The case for the market: Trump told the Financial Times “We seem to be getting everything we want”. [20]
aperture.weak: The people with flashlights near Sępopol who went back into Kaliningrad, the night after SACEUR's warning reached Warsaw. [48] Confirmation that it is a pattern: a second Polish or Lithuanian report of probing at the Kaliningrad line this week, or a NATO statement naming it.

number.t: Autonomous and counter-unmanned systems the DRPM-UxS says it delivered to the CENTCOM area this year. [75]

aperture.inject: STARTEX + 2, 23:40. Polish Border Guard reports about ten people crossing from the Kaliningrad oblast near Sępopol; a county emergency centre loses its radio net for 40 minutes. Stresses baseline requirements 3 (uncontrolled movement of people) and 6 (resilient communications). First calls: the Polish liaison for the national response, then the J2 for whether the Lithuanian side shows the same activity.
aperture.question: When SACEUR passes a threat warning to a host nation through national channels, as Tusk describes, how does JFC Brunssum learn what that nation then deployed, and how fast?

deep.title: Attritable, explained
body: An attritable system is built cheaply enough to lose. It is meant to come back, but its loss ends neither the mission nor the budget line. Adam Smith's 4 Nov letter to colleagues asked for “an appropriate mix of high-end survivable systems and lower-cost attritable capabilities”, and the word now appears in budgets on both sides of the Atlantic. [87]

This week's numbers: more than 25,000 drones and counter-drone systems delivered to CENTCOM this year; two experimental uncrewed combat aircraft in Germany's CFSN programme, worth more than €220 million; a Lithuanian plan for a state drone company. [75, 65, 61] For a planner the shift is in the arithmetic: an attritable fleet is counted in production rate and resupply time, not tail numbers, so the logistics annex shows how much of it is left on day ten.

longread.title: Cancellations, investigations, and even impeachment could be ahead under Democratic Congress
longread.why: Meghann Myers on what a Democratic Congress means for Golden Dome, Golden Fleet and AUTOWARCOM, with Todd Harrison and Mark Cancian. [77]

cards: Up 1,569.40 points, best day since April 2025
Ahold +6.6% on results; ASML, ASMI, Besi −5%+
money.driver: The Democratic sweep set off a broad rally: the Dow gained 1,569.40 points, its best day since April 2025. [89] Brent fell 8.7% and WTI 8.3%; Andy Lipow of Lipow Oil Associates: “The elections are leading the market to conclude that Trump might now be inclined to make a deal.” [86] In Amsterdam Ahold Delhaize rose 6.6% on third-quarter results while ASMI, ASML and Besi fell more than 5%. [90] US data held up: ADP counted 86,000 new private jobs in October and the ISM services index slipped to 54.5, with prices at 73.0. [93, 94] After the close Qualcomm fell about 6.5% on its outlook. [89] The 10-year Treasury yield eased to 4.90%. [92] Closes are from Yahoo Finance. [88]
rates: Held 28 Oct by 10–2; Cook and Hammack wanted a hike. [95]
Decision today 13:00 CET; a hike to 4% widely expected, Goldman sees a 7–2 vote. [4]

items.h: The tax-plan debate ends past midnight with a thin Kamer majority in sight
items.body: The Tweede Kamer debated the 2027 tax plan until 00:37 on Thursday; NOS says ChristenUnie, 50Plus and Groep Markuszower now appear to back it, enough for a small majority, while a majority in the Eerste Kamer is “ver weg”, far away. [102, 103] PVV leader Geert Wilders said his party will vote against the plan and every budget. [102] The cabinet answers the amendments on Tuesday 10 Nov and the Kamer votes on Thursday 12 Nov. [102]
items.fy: The 2027 fuel-duty discount is settled only when both chambers have voted; the Eerste Kamer takes the plan in December.

items.h: Nitrogen plans could close 10–30% more livestock farms, researchers find
items.body: A first analysis by Wageningen researchers for the agriculture ministry, led by Petra Berkhout, finds Minister Van Essen's nitrogen plans would make 10–30% more livestock farms stop; with about 10% stopping anyway, there would be 20–40% fewer by 2035. The plans require a 42–46% cut in ammonia; the researchers say food security is not at risk. [104]

items.h: Five consumer bodies warn against doorstep sales of batteries and heat pumps
items.body: The competition authority ACM, the Consumentenbond, the Fraudehelpdesk, Juridisch Loket and Vereniging Eigen Huis warned on 2 Nov against aggressive phone and doorstep sales of solar panels, home batteries and heat pumps; home batteries get no national subsidy. ACM board member Manon Leijten: “Daarom zijn dit soort producten niet geschikt voor verkoop aan de telefoon of aan de deur.” [105]
items.fy: Anything agreed at the door or by phone can be cancelled free within 14 days; the joint advice is “Hang op of sluit de deur”, hang up or close the door. [105]

otd.title: On this day · 5 November 1944
otd.body: Just before dawn the first infantry supplies since the loss of Schmidt reached the 112th Infantry's battalions at Kommerscheidt over the Kall trail, while German shelling and attacks went on. That afternoon Maj. Gen. Norman Cota ordered Task Force Ripple to retake Schmidt the next day. Kommerscheidt lies in the Hürtgen Forest, about 40 km from Heerlen. [120]

culture.title: The intocht: Sinterklaas comes to town
culture.body: Each November Sinterklaas arrives by steamboat for a national intocht, then makes local arrivals town by town until pakjesavond, the present-giving evening of 5 Dec. Parkstad's dates are set by permit: Heerlen at De Bongerd on Sun 15 Nov and Hoensbroek on the Gebrookerplein on Sat 21 Nov, while Brunssum has applied for the same Saturday. [109, 108, 121] In between, children leave a shoe by the door or the fireplace at night and find a small present or pepernoten in the morning.
